speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Health with the rise of flu-like human metapneumovirus (HMPV) cases in China (a) how does the Government ensure that cross-border transmission of HMPV will not pose public health concerns in Singapore; (b) whether the subsidised flu vaccination under Healthier SG is sufficient for the prevention of the spread of HMPV to seniors; and (c) what is being done to protect children, especially those aged 14 and below who are amongst those most affected by HMPV.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) how many cases of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) have been detected to date; (b) which are the age groups most severely affected by HMPV; (c) whether there are any fatalities due to HMPV; and (d) what measures have been implemented to reduce the number of infections in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The symptoms are similar to a common cold.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HMPV surges are common during the colder months in temperate regions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There have been significant surges in some parts of Asia this winter.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Minister of State for the reply.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When I raised this Parliamentary Question after reading about the HMPV cases rising in China in early January, I would never have expected that my own mom will be hospitalised due to HMPV for three days just before our Chinese New Year reunion dinner.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am grateful that her symptoms were picked up by an ear, nose and throat (ENT) specialist for a consultation that is actually unrelated to flu.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The good news is that she made it out from the hospital to join us for the reunion dinner.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One is that I used to receive from the Ministry of Health (MOH), SMSes to citizens, like myself, a reminder to enrol on the Healthier SG, a reminder to get the vaccine booster for COVID-19 when cases rose.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And the last SMS that I received would have been around May.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I wonder if MOH can consider sending similar SMS when there is a new flu variant or a flu that is increasing in cases overseas, so that citizens can be more aware of what are the protections that need to be done?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Those who are 40 to 65, for example, with high cholesterol, will not get a free flu vaccine.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, just a couple of days ago, it was reported in the news that a high-profile, 48-year-old Taiwanese celebrity died unexpectedly from a flu complication when holidaying in Japan.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I wonder if MOH can review the age criteria for the free annual flu vaccine and also include respiratory chronic diseases that is in remission, such as those who are on Healthier SG and did not report about a chronic disease that is in remission, like childhood asthma.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In general, the approach that we take is that we do want to focus on those interventions which have some evidence that they are going to have a significant effect on the health outcomes downstream.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Something like a flu vaccine is something that you need to do on a regular basis.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is not something that you do once and then you are done for life.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It has to be topped up every year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the considerations are different compared to, for example, a vaccination like measles, mumps and rubella, where, maybe, you do it once in your lifetime and then it has a long effect across your life.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: She also had a suggestion about alerts for flu variants.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we do have to be judicious about when we send out alerts, so that there is something specific in terms of the action that the citizens can take, rather than just providing information.
